name: Sierra de la Madera (eastern slopes)
synopsis: Somewhere in Sonora her mate is caught in a trap and killed by men on horseback, after she refuses to leave him. Alone, she roams the eastern slopes of this range for a week and finds almost nothing to eat.

name: Crossing of the Bavispe
synopsis: She crosses the Bavispe and turns north. She is pregnant for the first time, and she is leaving because the other wolves are gone, not the game.

name: The border at 108°30′ W
synopsis: She crosses into New Mexico where the boundary meets this meridian, and a mile on she crosses the old Nations road.

name: Whitewater Creek
synopsis: She follows the creek west and climbs with it into the San Luis Mountains.

name: San Luis Mountains
synopsis: She crosses the range and goes north through its gap towards the Animas Mountains. The book names the range only in passing.

name: Animas Mountains
synopsis: She passes through the Animas range on her way north. The book names it only in passing.

name: Animas Valley
synopsis: She crosses the valley floor towards the Peloncillos. Later, at night, she comes down onto these plains to run the antelope, watching the herd for a weak one.

name: Foster Draw (the calf)
synopsis: After two weeks of living on carrion she pulls down a calf in deep snow where the draw begins, and eats until she can hardly move. She never goes back to a kill, and she now keeps strict rules about roads, rail lines and fences.

name: Skeleton Creek, south fork
synopsis: She ranges west into Arizona and crosses the south fork of the creek.

name: Starvation Canyon
synopsis: She works west to the head of the canyon, still finding no sign of other wolves.

name: Hog Canyon Springs
synopsis: She turns south as far as the springs before heading back east. Later Billy tracks her as she crosses back towards Hog Canyon after killing a heifer.

name: Between Clanton and Foster draws
synopsis: Back in the high country she smells another wolf at one of the Parhams' trap sets and spends an hour reading the ground. Over the next day she digs out all eight sets and leaves the traps bare for Billy and his father to find.

name: Up Cloverdale Creek
synopsis: She keeps coming back to dig in the ashes of the vaqueros' noon fire, where Billy has buried a trap. One morning she is caught in it by her right forefoot.

name: Cloverdale
synopsis: Billy rides out before his father is awake and passes through Cloverdale at first light, then turns west up the creek road to check his set.

name: Cloverdale Creek road
synopsis: Billy finds the wolf in the trap and, instead of fetching his father, ropes her, wedges a stick in her jaws and ties her mouth shut. He frees her ruined foot, loses his horse while she fights the rope, and an old rancher in a Model A catches it for him.

name: Robertson's crossfence
synopsis: Leading the wolf home along the road, Billy stops for a long time at the crossfence, an hour short of Cloverdale. Then he turns off the road and heads south across open country towards Mexico.

name: Low pass in the easternmost Guadalupes
synopsis: At midday Billy and the wolf cross a low pass at the eastern end of the Guadalupes and ride down the open valley. Riders far off on the plain pass them by.

name: Ranch house on the volcanic plain
synopsis: At a ranch on the last fence before the line, three hounds rush the wolf and Billy's horse bolts. The rancher shuts her in the smokehouse, feeds Billy supper, and has an old Mexican stitch and dress her leg. Billy leaves at dark with food, a blanket and a collar bearing the rancher's name.

name: The boundary, a monument in sight
synopsis: Billy camps in sleet south of a pass, and in the morning he feels the pups move inside her. Near noon they cross into Sonora, with a concrete boundary marker standing off to the east.

name: Up the Cajón Bonito
synopsis: On the main trail south Billy passes a ruined waystation, and that night he finds the wolf has slipped her mouth ties, so he cuts her a muzzle from saddle leather. Her scent stampedes a burro train, an old woman and a girl warn him she will need her mouth free when the pups come, and five armed riders try to buy her.

name: Passes of the Sierra de la Cabellera
synopsis: Snow lies in the high passes, printed with the tracks of travellers who leave the trail when a rider comes. Billy camps in a stone ravine, and next day from a gap above the Bavispe valley he shares a meal with Indian miners carrying a dead companion home.

name: The river crossing (the deputies)
synopsis: Billy tries to swim the wolf across the Bavispe towards the Pilares Teras, but the current and the muzzle nearly drown her and his horse gets away. Two armed men watch from the gravel bar, ask for his papers, and take him downriver.

name: The mud-house settlement
synopsis: In a crumbling settlement of mud houses the alguacil seizes the wolf as contraband and lets Billy go because of his age. A deputy hauls her off in a mule cart, and Billy learns from the people following it that she is bound for the fair at Morelos.

name: Colonia Morelos (the fair)
synopsis: Billy reaches the old Mormon town with the fairgoers and finds the wolf chained in a cart under a sheet, shown for ten centavos. The man at the tent lets him in free, and Billy promises her he will take her to the mountains. Then the alguacil's hunting party rides into town and the cart is hurried away.

name: The hacienda
synopsis: Billy follows the hunting party to a hacienda on the Batopito, where the wolf is set to fight relays of dogs in a pit. He walks in, pulls the dogs off and claims her, but is forced at gunpoint to chain her again. He rides away, turns back, shoots her himself, and trades his rifle for her body.

name: Into the Pilares Teras
synopsis: Billy fords the river after dark with the wolf's body across his saddle and rides west all night, singing. At the foot of the Pilares he washes the blood out of the sheet and waits by a fire for daylight to bury her.
